title: Union-find and connectivity

objectives.text: Maintain a partition with representative equality, root sizes and successful-merge component counts.
Explain how path compression changes representation without changing connectivity, and distinguish amortized bounds from per-call latency.
Parse signed hundredths exactly and filter every edge with strict comparison.
Return all components including isolates with canonical member/group ordering.
Prove safe acceptance by a light-cut-edge exchange.
Handle self/parallel edges, disconnected/singleton output and wide total cost.

blocks.markdown: A disjoint-set structure maintains a partition of known elements into non-overlapping sets. Initially IDs 0 through n-1 each form a singleton. find(x) returns a representative of the set containing x; union(a,b) merges the two sets if different. The representative is an implementation choice and can change after a merge. It is not automatically the smallest ID, first arrival, legal owner or business label. Compare representatives for equality, not a particular numeric value unless that is a separate maintained contract.

Represent each set by a rooted parent tree with parent[root]=root. Following parents reaches its representative. Only root size entries are authoritative; a size stored at a former root may be stale after attachment. Before merging, find both roots. If equal, return False and do not decrement the component count. Otherwise attach the smaller tree below the larger root, add sizes at the surviving root and decrement the number of components once.

blocks.caption: Expected output: True, True, False, True, 3, 3 on separate lines. Two successful merges reduce five components to three; the repeated connection changes no partition. All endpoint checks reject bool, negative and out-of-range IDs. find may mutate parent pointers by compression even though it returns the same connectivity information.

blocks.markdown: The first pass in find reaches the root. The second pass rewires every visited non-root vertex directly to that root while remembering the old next pointer. It changes the internal parent forest, not which elements are in the same set. A parent chain is not a path of original graph edges: union can connect representatives that were not the exact input edge endpoints. Do not use DSU parents to reconstruct a shortest graph route.

blocks.source:
# A valid parent forest before a find on element3.
parent = [0, 0, 1, 2]
root = 3
while parent[root] != root:
    root = parent[root]
vertex = 3
while parent[vertex] != vertex:
    following = parent[vertex]
    parent[vertex] = root
    vertex = following
print(root)
print(parent)
blocks.caption: Expected output: 0, then [0, 0, 0, 0]. Elements 3, 2 and 1 still belong to the same set as before; the paths are simply shorter. This isolated valid-forest trace illustrates compression; it is not a claim that the shown chain was produced by the union-by-size policy.

blocks.markdown: Without compression, attaching the smaller tree below the larger means a vertex whose depth increases joins a component at least twice as large as before. Its depth can therefore increase at most floor(log2(n)) times before the component contains all n elements. Compression only shortens these paths. Combining union by size/rank and compression gives a very slowly growing inverse-Ackermann amortized bound across a sequence of operations. That advanced bound is cited, not proved here; it is not a promise that every operation takes identical constant time or meets a production latency target.

For an undirected network with additions only, each new edge can union its endpoints. A successful merge joins two previously disconnected components; an edge whose endpoints already share a representative is redundant for connectivity. With parallel edges or self-loops it may still be a distinct business event. DSU does not preserve the full edge log. If deletions can split components, ordinary DSU cannot undo them correctly just by changing one parent pointer.

This implementation is not a rollback or persistent DSU, a directed strong-connectivity algorithm, a path-distance index or an authenticated identity registry. Concurrent mutations need their own synchronization contract. A snapshot of parent arrays is also representation-specific; stable external component labels require a declared mapping. Keep the original event history separately when replay or audits require it.

Independent transfer: compare DSU connectivity and component sizes to a plain set-partition oracle after each small merge. Include repeated unions, self-unions, isolated elements and invalid endpoints. Check that root sizes sum to n and that the component counter equals the number of distinct representatives. Snapshot before a find and confirm that compression can change parents while preserving every pairwise connectivity answer. Explain why deleting an input edge is not supported by this interface.

Reference: [Disjoint Set Union](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/disjoint_set_union.html) for parent forests, union by size and compression. The logarithmic depth argument is explained here; the inverse-Ackermann sequence bound is an externally established theorem, not a learner proof completed by running this example. All network semantics are synthetic.

Exact link predicate

There are 1 to 100000 assets, labeled 0..n-1, and 0 to 200000 edge observations. The supplied parser passes theta and rho as two-decimal strings, not floats. rho is in [-1.00,1.00]. Form magnitude=100*whole+fractional, then apply the sign to the entire magnitude. Thus -0.20 is -20 and -0.00 is 0. Compare rho>theta: equality does not create a link. This parses guaranteed two-decimal text, not arbitrary numeric notation.

DSU invariant after filtering

After each edge prefix, DSU sets are precisely the components of accepted links from that prefix. A rejected line changes nothing; an accepted line unions its endpoints. Duplicate pairs are evaluated per line: a rejected observation does not cancel a later accepted one. Already-connected or reverse links are idempotent. Connectivity is transitive even if the endpoint pair itself has a low observed correlation. The complete block includes iterative path compression and union by size from the core invariant.

Roots are not output order

Union by size chooses structural representatives, not minimum member IDs. Visit every vertex in ascending order, including isolates, find its final root and append it to that bucket. Members are then increasing. Sort buckets by their first member, not root ID. Return the count line, then space-joined members.

With theta=0.50, accept 0-1 at 0.80 and 1-2 at 0.55; reject 3-4 at 0.50 and 0-2 at -0.20. Output the triple 0,1,2, then singleton 3, then singleton 4.

Work and independent transfer

DSU uses O(n) storage and amortized inverse-Ackermann work per operation by the cited theorem, not constant worst-case latency. Group sorting adds O(k log k); input/output storage is O(n+m), with formatting proportional to emitted digits. Independently construct the accepted graph with exact rational predicates and flood its components. Include equality, signed zero, negative thresholds, duplicates, isolates and maximum dimensions. These are connectivity clusters, not pairwise-all-correlated groups or certified risk models.

blocks.caption: Expected ['3', '0 1 2', '3', '4'], then ['1', '0 1']. Complete exact filter, DSU and canonical output.

blocks.markdown: Mechanism reference: [DSU representation, merge and compression](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/disjoint_set_union.html). Exact signed-hundredths parsing, the strict per-line filter and canonical all-vertex output are declared and derived task choices. The DSU source does not establish a correlation model or this numeric parser. Exact public task contract hash eb6926392b832f11d59bf10bb8ca152e550acb29a28a1176d49b2108111d52b1. This is teaching/source fit, not current app or judge sign-off.

Spanning backbone contract

There are 1 to 200000 vertices, labeled from 0, and 0 to 200000 undirected edges with weights 1..1e9. Parallel and self-edges are allowed. mst_weight(n,edges) returns a list containing one string: the minimum spanning total, or -1 if disconnected. The supplied main prints that string as one line. A singleton needs no links and has total 0 even with self-links. Minimize the selected link sum, not shortest-path distances.

Forest invariant

Sort a copy of the edges by ascending weight. DSU components equal the components of the selected forest. Same-root endpoints form a cycle or self-link, so skip them. Otherwise union the roots, add the weight and increment selected. Each acceptance reduces the component count by 1. n-1 accepted edges form a spanning tree. Ties may change chosen edges, not minimum total. Parallel edges compete normally; they are not summed together.

Cut exchange proof

For connected input, maintain a chosen forest A contained in some MST. The next accepted edge e crosses a cut S defined by one current component; no edge of A crosses it. Edge e is lightest across that cut: an earlier crossing edge would already have joined components.

If an MST T containing A omits e, adding e creates one cycle with another crossing edge f not in A. Since w(e)<=w(f), replace f by e. The result is still a spanning tree, costs no more, and preserves A. Thus some MST contains A+e. Ties are allowed; not every MST must contain every light edge.

Disconnected input, work and bounds

After all edges, selected<n-1 means no available edge crosses the remaining components, so return -1, not the forest cost. Sorting costs O(m log(m+1)); the DSU sequence costs O((n+m) alpha(n)) by the cited amortized theorem. Storage is O(n+m) including the copy. Connected cost<=(n-1)*1e9<=199999000000000 needs 64-bit C++ accumulation or exact Python integers. Iterative find avoids recursion. The output does not request selected edges.

Trace and independent transfer

For 0-1 cost 1, 1-2 cost 2, 0-2 cost 2, 2-3 cost 5, and 1-3 cost 4: accept weight 1, accept one weight 2, skip the resulting cycle, then accept weight 4. The total is 7. Enumerate n-1-edge subsets on tiny graphs, check connectivity, and minimize the sum independently of DSU. Include a singleton, m=0, disconnected graphs, self-links, unequal parallel links, equal-weight cycles, a maximum chain and wide weights. This does not establish remote judge/runtime qualification.

blocks.caption: Expected ['7'], ['-1'], ['0']. Safe forest with iterative DSU and disconnected check.

blocks.markdown: Algorithm references: [Berkeley cut lemma and Kruskal exchange proof](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/%7Edaw/teaching/cs170-s03/Notes/lecture8.pdf) and [DSU representation and amortized bound](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/disjoint_set_union.html). The positive input bounds, self/parallel-edge handling and disconnected -1/list-line adapter are specified here. The references do not certify runtime or output framing. summary: Maintain partition invariants, root-only sizes and successful-merge counts. Compression changes representation, not connectivity. Ordinary DSU handles merges, not arbitrary deletions, path reconstruction or directed strong components. Extension: exact threshold clusters. Extension: kruskal safe forest.
